decisions.diagnosis: Three runs of exact zeros in both directions (2021-03-01 to 03-17, 2021-04-27 to 05-01, 2021-05-10 to 07-11). They could be path closures for works or counter outages, so the automatic missing stays.
decisions.evidence: Nearby sites 184, 182 and 195 kept normal levels, so this is not weather. Zeros start at midnight Sunday into Monday and end on Mon 07:00, Sat 14:00 and Wed 16:00, and 184/182 rose from about 0.33 to 0.39 during the May-July run, which leans towards a closure. But the 2019 diversion here still let 1-10 bikes a day through, while these runs are 64 days of exact zeros.

decisions.diagnosis: Weekend with near-zero counts at 183 only. It could be a weekend closure or a counter fault; the automatic missing stays.
decisions.evidence: 183 raw 1/0 and 3/1, against 195 at 421-540 and 186 at 59-110; 183 was back to 43/27 on Monday.

series.name: Westbound
series.evidence: Same site and both labelled West. Counter 213 replaced 190 after a 4-day gap (2022-01-23 to 01-28). Levels are comparable: 190 averaged 30/day in Jan 2022 and 213 averaged 39-42/day in late Jan and 30 in Feb. Both West directions show the earlier 6-7am workday start.

series.name: Eastbound
series.evidence: Same site and both labelled East. Counter 213 replaced 190 after a 4-day gap. Levels are comparable: 190 averaged 34/day in Jan 2022 and 213 averaged 39/day in late Jan and 30 in Feb 2022.

summary: Site 183 is a single river-path leg. Counter 190 (2019-2022) was followed by counter 213 (2022-2024) with a 4-day gap and comparable levels, so the directions are joined by label. The May-June 2019 near-zero spell is a real diversion (site 185 tripled at the same time), and the level shifts in 2022-2023 are gradual and look real. Several automatic zero_outage fixes on storm and flood days are restored. The long exact-zero runs in 2021 could be closures or outages and stay missing, marked uncertain.
